name: Size · Straight Sets, Stretch Focus
summary: Six weeks of muscle building: chest & back, shoulders & arms, and legs, each twice a week. Same weight on every set, main lifts first, then supersets of non-competing muscles. Effort builds from week 1 to 5; week 6 is lighter.

insights.title: Goal
insights.body: Build muscle with moderate weights taken close to failure, at maintenance calories. Volume comes from your own history: extra side-delt and hamstring work (your slowest-moving areas), biceps trained early on arm days, about 18 weekly sets for chest and back, and every muscle gets at least one exercise that loads it in a deep stretch.

insights.title: How it works
insights.body: Each day has one job: chest and back (plus abs), then shoulders and arms, then legs, twice a week. Every set of an exercise uses the same weight and reps. The main lifts (30-degree incline dumbbell press, chest-supported T-bar row, Smith machine shoulder press, pendulum squat) come first, alone, with 2.5-3 minutes rest. The rest are supersets of muscles that don't compete, mostly at one station, like incline curls with dumbbell lateral raises: first exercise, about 10 seconds, second exercise, then the full rest.

insights.title: A days vs B days
insights.body: A days are heavier: 8 reps on the main lifts, 10 on the other compound lifts, 12 on isolation exercises and abs, and 15 on lateral raises, rear delts and calves. B days repeat the same exercises in the same order with lighter weights for 10, 12, 15 and 20 reps. Track and progress A and B days separately.

insights.title: How to progress
insights.body: The reps shown are your target. When every set reaches it with clean form at that week's effort, add the smallest step next time (about 1-2.5 kg upper body, 2.5-5 kg legs); if the last sets fall 1-2 reps short, keep the weight and beat it next week. Effort rises through the block: week 1 stop about 3 reps before failure, week 2 about 2, weeks 3-4 about 1-2, week 5 about 1, and only the last set of machine, cable or isolation work may go to failure.

insights.title: What to expect
insights.body: Week 1 should feel easy on purpose while you find your weights and learn the new exercises. Weeks 2-5 get harder each week and should bring more reps or weight on most lifts. Shoulder and arm days come the day after chest and back, so the shoulder press may feel slightly weaker than when fresh; that is normal. Week 6 is lighter: same exercises and weights, half the sets (round up), about 3 reps before failure.

insights.title: Key tips
insights.body: Set up before supersets: a flat bench next to the pulldown, dumbbells by the incline bench for curls and laterals, and one cable tower for fly, straight-arm pulldown and crunch. If the second machine of a pair is taken, do both as straight sets with the same rest. Lower slowly into every stretch without bouncing. Never grind squats, RDLs or presses to failure. If a movement hurts, stop it and see a qualified professional.
